rows.phenotypeRestriction: treatment-related urethral stricture after TURP or HoLEP for BPH
rows.citation: Chen F, Chen Y, Zou Y, Wang Y, Wu X, Chen M. Comparison of holmium laser enucleation and transurethral resection of prostate in benign prostatic hyperplasia: a systematic review and meta-analysis. J Int Med Res. 2023;51(8):3000605231190763. PMID 37561537. doi:10.1177/03000605231190763.
rows.evidenceType: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
rows.proposition: Treatment-mediated urethral-stricture risk after TURP or HoLEP performed for documented benign prostatic hyperplasia.
rows.publicationGuard: Require documented benign prostatic hyperplasia, documented transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) or holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP), and a separately established urethral stricture arising after that procedure with compatible chronology. Do not infer urethral stricture from untreated BPH, lower urinary tract symptoms, or bladder-outlet obstruction alone. Preserve prior urethral instrumentation or trauma, infection, lichen sclerosus, prior pelvic surgery or radiation, and other recognized causes of urethral stricture.

rows.citation: Alende-Castro V, Macía-Rodríguez C, Novo-Veleiro I, et al. Q fever in Spain: Description of a new series, and systematic review. PLoS Negl Trop Dis. 2018;12(3):e0006338. PMID 29543806. doi:10.1371/journal.pntd.0006338.
rows.proposition: Acute Q-fever-associated hepatitis or hepatic injury as a recognized acute manifestation/complication.
rows.publicationGuard: Require clinically established acute Q fever using appropriate Coxiella burnetii diagnostic evidence and separately established acute hepatitis or hepatic injury with compatible timing. Do not generalize this edge to chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, or an isolated nonspecific liver-enzyme elevation without a compatible acute Q-fever syndrome. Preserve viral hepatitis, alcohol-associated liver disease, metabolic liver disease, autoimmune hepatitis, drug- or toxin-induced injury, ischemic injury, biliary disease, and other hepatic causes.

rows.phenotypeRestriction: hemodynamically confirmed MPN-associated precapillary PH, including CTEPH or group-5 PH
rows.citation: Montani D, Thoré P, Mignard X, et al. Clinical Phenotype and Outcomes of Pulmonary Hypertension Associated with Myeloproliferative Neoplasms: A Population-based Study. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2023;208(5):600-612. PMID 37311222. doi:10.1164/rccm.202210-1941OC.
rows.proposition: Hemodynamically established pulmonary hypertension associated with myeloproliferative neoplasms, including PV-associated CTEPH/group-5 phenotypes.
rows.publicationGuard: Require confirmed polycythemia vera and a separately established pulmonary-hypertension diagnosis using appropriate hemodynamic evaluation, with classification of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension versus group-5 or other PH mechanisms. Do not infer pulmonary hypertension from polycythemia vera, dyspnea, hypoxemia, or an isolated echocardiographic estimate alone. Treat the registry as population-level complication evidence rather than automatic individual causation. Preserve left-heart disease, chronic lung disease or hypoxia, sleep-disordered breathing, unrelated thromboembolic disease, medications, and other recognized pulmonary-hypertension causes.

rows.phenotypeRestriction: physiologically relevant/sliding hiatal hernia with separately established GERD
rows.citation: Fein M, Ritter MP, DeMeester TR, et al. Role of the lower esophageal sphincter and hiatal hernia in the pathogenesis of gastroesophageal reflux disease. J Gastrointest Surg. 1999;3(4):405-410. PMID 10482693. doi:10.1016/S1091-255X(99)80057-2.
rows.evidenceType: clinical physiologic cohort with multivariable analysis
rows.proposition: Physiologically relevant hiatal hernia as an anatomic contributor to objectively established gastroesophageal reflux disease.
rows.publicationGuard: Require a documented hiatal hernia, with the source proposition most directly applicable to a sliding or otherwise physiologically relevant gastroesophageal-junction hernia, and a separately established diagnosis of GERD using appropriate clinical, endoscopic, or reflux-monitoring evidence. Do not infer GERD solely from the presence of a hiatal hernia. Preserve lower-esophageal-sphincter dysfunction, obesity, medications, delayed gastric emptying, dietary or behavioral contributors, prior foregut surgery, and other reflux causes.

rows.phenotypeRestriction: treatment-related myocardial dysfunction/cardiomyopathy after esophageal-cancer chemoradiotherapy
rows.citation: Søndergaard MMA, Nordsmark M, Møller DS, Nielsen KM, Poulsen SH. Reduction in myocardial function and oxygen consumption after chemoradiotherapy in patients with esophageal cancer. Acta Oncol. 2022;61(5):566-574. PMID 35289694. doi:10.1080/0284186X.2022.2048068.
rows.proposition: Treatment-mediated myocardial dysfunction/cardiomyopathy following actual thoracic chemoradiotherapy for esophageal cancer.
rows.publicationGuard: Require documented esophageal cancer, actual exposure to thoracic chemoradiotherapy, and a separately established myocardial-dysfunction or cardiomyopathy phenotype with compatible post-treatment chronology. Do not infer cardiomyopathy from the cancer diagnosis, radiation exposure, a small isolated strain change, fatigue, or dyspnea alone. Preserve pre-existing cardiomyopathy or heart failure, ischemic disease, hypertension, valvular disease, arrhythmia, other cardiotoxic therapies, alcohol or toxin exposure, genetic cardiomyopathy, and other recognized myocardial causes.
